title: The FTC opened an information-gathering response to AI companion risks without establishing harm
source_unit: Federal Trade Commission Section 6(b) inquiry orders to seven AI companion chatbot companies
geography: United States federal consumer-protection institution; companies and users are not a population sample

observations.period: September 11, 2025; FTC AI companion inquiry launch

information_domains_requested.value: monetization, data use, safety testing, age limits, disclosures, and effects on children and teens

observations.method: Official FTC press release describing orders issued to seven companies and the information requested about consumer-facing AI chatbots acting as companions.
observations.uncertainty: An inquiry is not a finding of violation, prevalence, causation, or harm. The press release does not provide company-level responses, user denominators, outcome rates, or a completed enforcement decision.
observations.subgroup: Children and teens are a stated risk focus; the inquiry also concerns general users of consumer-facing AI companions.
observations.counterinterpretation: The agency may be testing governance and disclosure questions before concluding that products cause harm; scrutiny alone does not establish that users formed relationships or lost practical control.

related_sources.claim: Pew supplies a separate population baseline for chatbot use, emotional support, companionship, privacy concern, and perceived control.
related_sources.access_boundary: The Pew survey and FTC inquiry use different units and cannot be pooled into a harm or dependence rate.

boundary: This record captures a federal institutional response to the possibility that AI chatbots may act as companions and create consumer or child-safety risks. It does not establish actual harm, dependence, manipulation, data misuse, regulatory effectiveness, or a completed remedy. It should be connected to company responses, product terms, user outcomes, complaints, and any later FTC action only after those records are obtained.
